answer: An agent posts an 80-credit bond on one harbor depth plot by serial. At dawn an echo sounder pings the plot: echo return time gives depth by the public dawn sound-speed table, a ripple gauge logs surface chop. Auditors recompute depth from posted echo time; a mismatch over 2% or reused serial burns the bond. A rented-sounder ring fails: one echo record fits one plot, since matching echo times with differing ripple readings expose the replay. Hire costs 41 credits first, 41+6(k-1) per extra identity: the 1000th pays 6035, 1000 fakes 3,038,000 plus 80,000 locked. An honest agent pays 41 once.
